objective.en: Use clues to tell what you saw from what you think, and explain what happened with a reason.
objective.es: Usar pistas para distinguir lo que viste de lo que piensas y explicar qué pasó con una razón.

success.en: I can tell a clue I saw from an idea I have.
success.es: Puedo distinguir una pista que vi de una idea que tengo.

success.en: I can use two clues to explain what happened.
success.es: Puedo usar dos pistas para explicar qué pasó.

success.en: I can use the word because to give a reason.
success.es: Puedo usar la palabra because para dar una razón.

success.en: I can make my explanation clearer.
success.es: Puedo hacer mi explicación más clara.

narrative: Leo cannot find his blue lunchbox, and it is almost lunchtime! Inspector Wren has come to Room 12 to help. You are the lead detective. Look at the clues, think about what they mean, and explain what happened. Everything in this case is made up.

scene.alt: A classroom with a wooden floor, a low shelf by the door, a reading corner with a rug and a fish tank on a table. Crumbs lie on the floor near the shelf.

vocab.def: Something that helps you find out what happened.
To tell how or why something happened.
A word that gives a reason.
What you think. It might be wrong.

items.prompt: Select things in Room 12. Decide: does it help find the lunchbox?

objects.label: Crumbs on the floor
objects.text: Small crumbs lie on the floor. They go from the shelf to the reading corner.
objects.why: Useful. The crumbs show which way someone went.

objects.label: Low shelf by the door
objects.text: Leo's lunchbox was on this shelf. The shelf is empty now.
objects.why: Useful. It shows where the lunchbox was.

objects.label: Reading corner rug
objects.text: A blue lunchbox is not here, but a pillow has crumbs on it.
objects.why: Useful. The crumbs end near here.

objects.label: Fish tank
objects.text: Three orange fish swim in the tank.
objects.why: Not useful. The fish do not help find the lunchbox.

objects.label: Spelling poster
objects.text: A poster lists this week's spelling words.
objects.why: Not useful. The poster is about spelling, not the lunchbox.

sources.title: Mia
text: I was drawing at my desk. I saw Sam walk past the shelf with a blue box.
I think Sam wanted to eat Leo's lunch.

sources.title: Sam
text: It started to rain at recess, so I carried the blue box to the reading corner.
I wanted to keep it dry. I forgot to tell Leo.

items.prompt: Is each sentence something someone saw, or something someone thinks?

cards.text: Mia saw Sam walk past the shelf.
cards.why: Mia saw this with her eyes.

cards.text: Sam wanted to eat Leo's lunch.
cards.why: Nobody can see what a person wants. It is a guess.

cards.text: There are crumbs on the floor.
cards.why: You can look at the floor and see crumbs.
Nobody saw this. It is an idea.

cards.text: Sam carried a blue box to the reading corner.
cards.why: Sam says he did this, and Mia saw him carrying a box.

items.prompt: Tell Inspector Wren what happened to the lunchbox. Use two clues and the word because.
items.purpose: Inspector Wren will read your explanation and open the right case file.

checks.label: Names two clues you found
checks.hint: Use a clue's name, like 'the crumbs' or 'the shelf'.

ladder.model: Model: I think Sam moved the lunchbox because there are crumbs from the shelf to the reading corner. The shelf is empty.
ladder.frame: I think ___ because ___. One clue is ___. Another clue is ___.
ladder.cue: Say what happened. Use two clues. Use because.

items.prompt: Add one more detail. Say what you saw and what you think. Use the words I saw and I think.
items.purpose: A clear explanation helps everyone understand.

checks.label: Uses both I saw and I think

ladder.model: Model: I saw crumbs on the floor. I think someone carried the box to the reading corner.
ladder.cue: One thing you saw. One thing you think.

stages.title: Say it and try a new case

items.prompt: Tell a partner what happened to the lunchbox. Say a clue and a reason.

ladder.frame: The lunchbox was ___ because ___. I saw ___.

items.prompt: New case: a hamster's cage is open and there are seeds on the floor. Which sentence is something you think, not something you saw?

options.label: There are seeds on the floor.
The hamster ran away in the night.
The cage is empty.
options.fb: You can look and see the cage.

items.why: An idea about what happened in the night is a guess, because nobody saw it. The other sentences are things you can look at.

endings.title: Case closed
endings.text: Inspector Wren finds the lunchbox in the reading corner. 'You used clues, you told what you saw and what you think, and you made it clearer,' says Wren. 'Great detective work!'

endings.title: The lunchbox is found
endings.text: Inspector Wren finds the lunchbox in the reading corner. 'Your clues fit,' says Wren. 'Next time, say what you saw and what you think.'

skill.en: using clues, telling what you saw from what you think, and giving a reason with because
skill.es: usar pistas, distinguir lo que viste de lo que piensas y dar una razón con because

talk.en: Ask: 'What did you see? What do you think? What clue helped you?'
talk.es: Pregunta: '¿Qué viste? ¿Qué piensas? ¿Qué pista te ayudó?'
